The sinus node cells do not possess contractile capacity as they lack myofibrils and are specialized for conduction. Additionally, they do not exhibit a long plateau phase like cardiac myocytes. analysis: The cells of the sinoatrial (SA) node, which is the natural pacemaker of the heart, are characterized by their ability to spontaneously depolarize and generate action potentials. They do not have a stable resting membrane potential like other cardiac cells; instead, they exhibit a gradual depolarization due to the influx of sodium (Na+) and calcium (Ca2+) ions. This depolarization occurs faster than in Purkinje fibers, which are specialized for conduction rather than pacemaking. The depolarization in SA node cells is primarily mediated by calcium channels, particularly T-type calcium channels, rather than sodium channels.
